summary: An overview of this week's technology developments, highlighting advancements and regulations in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity breaches, open-source developer policies, and data center automation.

items.title: Debian won't ban AI code from its Linux distribution
items.summary: Debian developers voted to allow the use of generative AI tools in contributions for development, maintenance, and documentation. This decision acknowledges that responsible AI use can boost developer productivity without requiring special rules beyond existing standards.

items.title: Hackers claim millions of patient records stolen during data breach at healthcare giant McKesson
items.summary: Healthcare giant McKesson experienced a data breach where hackers claim to have stolen millions of patient records. The company, which distributes medical supplies across the U.S., warned of potential intermittent service degradation following the hack.

items.title: ChatGPT to face tougher regulation in the EU
items.summary: The European Union has designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine under the Digital Services Act, subjecting it to strict online safety rules. OpenAI will now be legally required to mitigate risks concerning minors, user mental health, and illegal content.

items.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
items.summary: Meta is testing robots in its data centers to perform tasks typically handled by human technicians. This initiative aims to automate operations and improve efficiency within the company's massive infrastructure.

items.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
items.summary: Instagram is restricting the reach of undisclosed AI profiles in response to growing user frustration over AI influencers. The platform aims to enforce transparency by limiting the visibility of accounts that do not disclose their AI nature.
